Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:6: And in the Zohar (Parashat Bereishit, end, page 56) they were also strict concerning the punishment for this sin - these are its words: Rabbi Yehudah opened (Psalms 5:5), "for You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil shall not sojourn with You" - this verse has been stated and established, but come and see: whoever cleaves to the evil inclination and is drawn after it becomes impure, as it is said (Genesis 6:5), "for the evil of man was great" - they did all evils, and their sin was not complete until they spilled seed in vain upon the earth - and who are they? Those who corrupted their way upon the earth - this is what is written, "only evil all the day" - it is written here, "only evil," and it is written there, "evil shall not sojourn with You," and it is written (Genesis 38:7), "and Er, the firstborn of Judah, was evil in the eyes of the LORD."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:7: Rabbi Yosei said, but is not "evil" the same as "wicked"? He said to him, no - a wicked person is called such even if he merely raises his hand against his fellow, although he does not actually harm him at all, as it is written (Exodus 2:13), "and he said to the wicked one, why do you strike your fellow?" - it is not written "you struck," but "you strike" [i.e., merely raising the hand suffices for the term]. But "evil" [ra] is called only one who corrupts his way and defiles himself and defiles the land, and gives strength and power to the impure spirit called "evil" - as it is written, "only evil all the day" - and he does not enter the palace and does not see the face of the Shechinah, because through this the Shechinah departs from the world. From where do we know this? From Jacob - for when the Shechinah departed from him, he thought there was disqualification among his sons, because of whom the impure spirit was strengthened and diminished the light from the moon and blemished it. And if you say, why? Because that one defiled the sanctuary and the Shechinah departed from upon Jacob - all the more so one who corrupts his own way and defiles himself, for he strengthens the impure spirit, and therefore, when he becomes impure, he is called "evil." Come and see: when a person becomes impure, he is never remembered for good, and at every time he is remembered from that which is called "evil," for evil - this is what is written (Proverbs 19:23), "and satisfied, he shall lodge, not visited by evil" - when he walks the straight path, then he is "not visited by evil," and therefore it is written, "only evil all the day," and it is written, "evil shall not sojourn with You" - and behold, he is called "evil" and not "wicked" - and it is written (Psalms 23:4), "even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I shall fear no evil, for You are with me" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:8: Behold, his punishment is explained: that he does not see the face of the Shechinah and does not enter the palace, and this is because of the causes mentioned in the teaching. The first, that it said, "he defiles himself" - by arousing, in all his organs, the spirit of impurity, through the power of that very boiling by which he heated himself, since it is impossible for the drop of seed to come out except through the heating of all the organs - it follows that his organs become impure. And this resembles somewhat the sin of anger, as explained in Parashat Tetzaveh (page 182b), that one who boils with anger makes himself impure, within and without.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:9: And therefore it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayeshev, page 188a) that there is no sin by which a person becomes as impure as the sin of seed in vain - these are its words: and come and see, among all those sins by which a person becomes impure in this world, this is the sin by which a person becomes more impure, in this world and in the World to Come, than any other: whoever spills his seed emptily, and emits his seed emptily by hand or by other means, and becomes impure through it, as it is said (Psalms 5:5), "for You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil shall not sojourn with You" - therefore he does not enter behind the curtain and does not see the countenance of the Ancient of Days, as we have learned - it is written here, "evil shall not sojourn with You," and it is written there, "and Er, the firstborn of Judah, was evil in the eyes of the LORD" - and therefore (Isaiah 1:15), "your hands are full of blood." Happy is the portion of the person who fears his Master, and shall be guarded from the evil way, and shall purify himself to occupy himself in the fear of his Master - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:10: It further said, "and he defiles the land" - meaning that he defiles the supernal land, and the reason is that the supernal land [Malchut] receives flow only from the supernal Tzaddik, and the Tzaddik bestows only into her - and when a person heats himself in vain, he causes the supernal covenant to be subjugated to bestow the good, supernal flow to the externals, for the secret of its establishment, in the secret of (Genesis 17:21), "and My covenant I will establish with Isaac," is through the arousal of Torah and good deeds, to bestow into it the light of the supernal whiteness - and when he is one who has a seminal emission through heating himself via Lilith and her powers, this too is in vain, and all that is empty and vain belongs to the externals, like a nation who bows to vanity and emptiness - it follows that the flow that was fit to be received by the mistress is received by the maidservant, so that "a maidservant inherits her mistress," and the mistress receives the leftover, which is the harsh judgment from the side of the left - and this is "and he defiles the land." And whoever knows the secret of the supernal union knows how severe this sin is.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:11: "And he gives strength and power to the impure spirit" - explained by what has been said. And therefore, measure for measure, just as the blemish was in the Shechinah, so he shall not receive the face of the Shechinah - and just as he gave dominion over himself to the spirit of impurity, so his soul shall not enter the palace, which is the secret of holiness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:12: And it said at the end of the teaching, come and see, when a person becomes impure he is not remembered - explained along the lines of what is explained in the Gemara, Tractate Berachot (14a): Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan, whoever satisfies himself with words of Torah and goes to sleep is not brought bad tidings, as it is said (Proverbs 19:23), "and satisfied, he shall lodge, not visited by evil" - to this point. And according to the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, this "evil" mentioned in the verse is one who emits seed in vain, and the meaning is that he shall not come to a nocturnal emission when he is satisfied with words of Torah, for words of Torah are a remedy for this affliction, as we shall further explain. And it meant, by saying "when a person becomes impure," and so on, that as long as he has not repented from this sin, he is not visited in his dream from the side of the Holy One, blessed be He, for good - on the contrary, since the externals rule over him, he is their portion, and they visit him with evil and make him impure with an emission - and this is what it said, "and at every time he is visited from that which is called 'evil' with harm."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:13: And especially if he wishes to enter into the inner wisdom, into the place of the secret, and he is blemished in the attribute of Tzaddik, which is the secret, he is pushed away from there, and they make him impure to show him that he is not fit to enter there - and so it is proven in the Zohar (Parashat Naso, page 123a). And so they said in the Tikkunim, Tikkun One (page 17b) - these are its words: "Bereishit" [in the beginning], two "beginnings" - "this is the gate of the LORD; the righteous shall enter through it" (Psalms 118:20) - this is the gate of the righteous, who have permission to enter there, and others who are not righteous are pushed away from there - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:14: Further, in the Zohar (Parashat Noach, page 62a): come and see, all of a person's sins - all his corruptions - depend on repentance, but the sin of one who spills his seed and corrupts his way and emits seed upon the ground corrupts himself and corrupts the land; of him it is written (Jeremiah 2:22), "your iniquity is engraved before Me," and it is written of him (Psalms 5:5), "for You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil shall not sojourn with You," and it is written (Genesis 38:7), "and Er, the firstborn of Judah, was evil in the eyes of the LORD, and the LORD put him to death" - and this has already been stated - to this point. And in some manuscript versions it is written: "except by the power of powerful repentance."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:15: Further, in the Zohar (Parashat Noach, beginning of page 69) - these are its words: among all the sins of the world's sinners that push away the Shechinah, one of them is one who corrupts his way upon the earth, as we have said, and therefore he does not see the face of the Shechinah and does not enter the palace - and therefore it is written concerning these (Genesis 7:23), "and they were wiped out from the earth" - they were wiped out entirely. Come and see, at the time the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to revive the dead, all those dead found outside, in other foreign lands, the Holy One, blessed be He, shall create their bodies as fitting, and so on, but the Holy One, blessed be He, gives them souls only in the land of Israel, as it is said (Ezekiel 37:12), "behold, I open your graves and bring you up from your graves, My people, and bring you to the land of Israel" - that they shall roll under the ground, and afterward what is written? (ibid. 37:14), "and I will put My spirit in you, and you shall live," and so on - for in the land of Israel all the people of the world shall receive souls, except those who defiled themselves and defiled the land - of these it is written, "and they were wiped out from the earth," precisely - and although the early ones disputed about this, "wiped out," as it is said (Psalms 69:29), "let them be wiped out from the book of life." Rabbi Shimon said to him, certainly they have no portion in the World to Come, as it is written, "and they were wiped out from the earth," and it is written (Isaiah 60:21), "they shall inherit the land forever" - but they shall arise for judgment, and of them it is said (Daniel 12:2), "and many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:16: And although this teaching speaks of the generation of the Flood, who have no portion in the World to Come, and, according to Rabbi Abba's view, shall not arise either in resurrection or for judgment - nevertheless we learn from it that whoever, in this generation, acts as they did and does not repent, shall have no portion in the World to Come; and if he does arise for judgment, according to the view of Rashbi, it shall be for disgrace - for since the essential reason given for the generation of the Flood having no portion in the World to Come was that they spilled their seed upon the earth, as it is written (Genesis 6:12), "for all flesh had corrupted its way upon the earth," and this caused them to be "wiped out from the earth" without qualification, both above and below - so it shall be for anyone who acts like them and does not repent.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:17: And in the Zohar (Parashat Vayechi, page 219b) it was also strict about the severity of this sin, on the verse (Isaiah 3:11), "woe to the wicked evildoer [rasha ra], for the recompense of his hands shall be done to him" - these are its words: why "for the recompense of his hands"? Rabbi Yitzchak said, to include one who fornicates with his hands, to emit and corrupt his seed emptily - he is called "evil" and does not see the face of the Shechinah, (Psalms 5:5) "for You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil shall not sojourn with You," and it is written (Genesis 38:7), "and Er, the firstborn of Judah, was evil" - here too, "woe to the wicked evildoer" - woe to that guilty one who is "evil," who makes himself evil - "for the recompense of his hands shall be done to him," to include one who fornicates with his hands, to emit and corrupt his seed emptily, and this one is banished in that world more than anyone. Come and see, it is written, "woe to the wicked evildoer" - why "evildoer"? Rather, as we have said, he makes himself evil - and it is written, "evil shall not sojourn with You," and all [other sinners] ascend [from Gehinnom eventually], but this one does not ascend. And if you say, what of other guilty ones who killed people - come and see, all of them ascend, but he does not ascend; why? Because they killed another person, but this one actually kills his own children, and spills much blood. Come and see, of other guilty ones of the world it is not written, "and it was evil in the eyes of the LORD," but here it is written (Genesis 38:10), "and what he did was evil in the eyes of the LORD" - why? Because it is written (ibid. 38:9), "and he spoiled it on the ground."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:18: We have learned: Rabbi Yehudah said, there is no sin in the world that has no repentance except this one, and there are no guilty ones who do not see the face of the Shechinah except these, as it is written, "evil shall not sojourn with You." Rabbi Yitzchak said, happy are the righteous in this world and in the World to Come; of them it is written (Isaiah 60:21), "and your people, all of them righteous, shall inherit the land forever," and so on - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:19: Although in this teaching it said, without qualification, that he has no repentance, we must resolve this matter, for we hold that there is nothing that has no repentance, since even Manasseh was accepted by the Holy One, blessed be He (Sanhedrin 103a) - if so, how does this sin differ from the rest?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:20: And it appears to me to resolve this: the intent is that the matter does not depend on lower repentance, as with other blemishes, whose beginning of return is through lower repentance, meaning that by turning away from evil they are immediately accepted - and so is precisely the language, juxtaposed: "and there are no guilty ones who do not see the face of the Shechinah except these." And the reason is that this sin is against the Tzaddik and the Shechinah together, as explained, and therefore, since the Shechinah is his accuser, she does not accept his repentance [in the ordinary way].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:21: For through this, the verse (Psalms 34:17) is understood: "the face of the LORD is against evildoers, to cut off their remembrance from the earth" - "they cried out, and the LORD heard" - for "evildoers" [osei ra] are those called ones who emit seed in vain, and they are cut off from the land of the living because the blemish is in her [the Shechinah]; but "they cried out" and returned in repentance, and "the LORD heard," and saved them from all their troubles - as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Shemot, page 20a): Rabbi Yehudah said, great is the cry that tears up a person's decree throughout all his days; Rabbi Yitzchak says, great is the cry that rules over the supernal attribute of judgment; Rabbi Yosei says, great is the cry that rules in this world and in the World to Come - through crying out one inherits this world and the World to Come, as it is said (Psalms 107:6), "and they cried out to the LORD in their distress, and He saved them from their afflictions" - to this point. It follows that the cry is above lower repentance, according to all these explanations, and therefore, "and the LORD heard" - and the intent is that his repentance is difficult, until he reaches upper repentance.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:22: And so the sage, His Honor Rabbi Yehudah Chalgua, peace be upon him, wrote in Sefer Tzafnat Pane'ach, that the intent in saying he has no repentance is that his repentance is exceedingly difficult, and it is not sufficient for him to do repentance, because he needs many mortifications, and the penitent shall grow weary and shall not do what is proper to do - this is what is meant by "he has no repentance." And further, along the lines of what they, of blessed memory, said (Avodah Zarah 17a), "all who go to her do not return," and so on (Proverbs 2:19), concerning one who has heresy, for whom it is difficult to abandon his way, and he shall not return.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:23: And there is support for this view from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him (Zohar, Parashat Vayakhel, page 214b), who was strict there concerning the severity of blemishing the sign of the covenant, and said at the end of his words, woe to that shame for which vengeance of the worlds is taken from him - the vengeance of this world and the vengeance of that blemish - and it said afterward, and these matters apply when he has not done a complete repentance, a repentance fitting to cover all his deeds - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:24: And the reason he needs a complete repentance to cover all his deeds is that the attribute of Tzaddik is called "all" [kol], since all the attributes are included in it, as explained in the Tikkunim (page 145b) - and likewise, the blemish in the covenant is a blemish in all the letters of YHVH, as explained in the Tikkunim (page 131a): Mem-Yud, "Yud shall ascend to us to heaven" - the acrostic is MILAH [circumcision], the final letters are YHVH - it follows that whoever blemishes the covenant blemishes all the attributes included in the attribute of Tzaddik, and in the letters of the Name, and it is as though he blemished the whole "measure of the stature" [shi'ur komah] - and for this he needs a complete repentance, fitting to cover all his deeds, for even though he has blemished all his organs, he needs to act to repair all his organs, as we shall explain. And now this may be resolved in another way: every repentance requires the repentance in the organ with which one sinned, but the sin in the covenant does not depend on the repentance of the covenant alone, such as marrying a woman, but rather requires a powerful repentance, as though he had blemished all his organs, as explained - and we shall elaborate further below.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:25: And a proof that even those who emit seed in vain have repentance is that the generation of the Flood were emitting their seed in vain, and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained that Noah was delayed in building the ark in order to announce to them that they should return and repent - they said in Midrash Tanchuma, Parashat Noach (siman 5): Rabbi Huna said in the name of Rabbi Yosei, for one hundred twenty years the Holy One, blessed be He, warned the generation of the Flood, [waiting to see] whether they would repent; since they did not, He said to Noah (Genesis 6:14), "make yourself an ark of gopher wood" - Noah stood and planted cedars - see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:26: And my teacher, peace be upon him, wrote in Sefer Elimah concerning the repentance for this sin, and I have summarized his words, which are as follows: we find that it is called "evil," and evil is the opposite of good - and the matter is that the Tzaddik is called "good," since he causes the light of Yesod to be drawn to the female, for there is the "outpouring of the streams" of seed, the supernal light - and since he bestows this in vain, Lilith is found there, who is called "empty and vain," and causes the supernal covenant to be subjugated to bestow to the externals, and causes "a maidservant to inherit her mistress" - for the flow that was fit to be bestowed to the Shechinah is bestowed to the externals - and therefore he is called "evil," and therefore he does not see the face of the Shechinah, meaning the hidden good bestowed to her - since he blemished her, he shall not merit that taste after entering Gehinnom, unlike other sinners, for other sinners, after the measure of their sin's punishment in Gehinnom is completed, enter the Garden of Eden to receive their reward - unlike one who blemished by emitting seed in vain. And there is no sin that makes a person's soul as impure as emitting seed in vain. And this is if he has not repented; however, if he repents, there is nothing that stands before repentance - and what is explained in the Zohar, that it does not depend on repentance, is that he needs to do things that are above the place of repentance. And the reason is that whoever blemishes the covenant blemishes the brain, since from there the seed is bestowed, and he blemishes Chochmah - and therefore he needs to do repentance above the place of repentance, which is Binah. And this repair needs three things: the first, repentance; the second, Chochmah; the third, humility. The repentance is to distance himself from evil and cleave to good, meaning that he shall perform adornments and unifications for the Shechinah, in a manner that what was separated from the Tzaddik shall gaze at her face toward him, and Yesod shall bestow into her. And likewise, the repentance is to mortify himself with great mortification and submission, in place of having heated himself, and through this he shall merit the attribute of humility, which is above the place of repentance - and there is nothing that is not repaired by its opposite. And likewise, when he merits Chochmah, and draws from Chochmah the light of Torah to Yesod, to bestow to Malchut, corresponding to the drops of seed drawn from the brain to the covenant. And likewise, in drawing the supernal secrets from the secret of Da'at to Yesod, this too repairs the blemish, for through this the Shechinah shines through Yesod, as explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, page 94a). The principle is that there is nothing that is not repaired by repentance, and what is explained in the Zohar, that it does not depend on repentance, means that his repentance is difficult - and this too is part of the difficulty of the repentance shown to him, that it does not depend on repentance, and yet there is nothing that stands before repentance. And even if you have heard, "return, wayward children" - except so-and-so, as with Elisha [ben Avuyah] "Acher" - do not be concerned, for Acher, in the end, was accepted even though he did not repent (Chagigah 15b); all the more so had he repented it would have benefited him far more - it was only that the doors of repentance were closed before him, and he needed to plead until the door opened - and this is what they, of blessed memory, said (Pesachim 86b), whatever the master of the house tells you to do, do, except "leave." "Master of the house" refers to the Holy One, blessed be He - whatever mitzvah He tells you to do, do; except "leave" - if He tells you, leave My house and do not enter, as with Elisha Acher, do not listen to him, but rather enter through repentance, for this is the master of the house's true desire, only that He is testing you.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:27: And one must persist in repentance year after year, and not forget how many times he angered his Creator, for all his sins are counted and written - and if not, Lilith is ready to collect from him the sum of his sins, [for] wherever he heated himself between her thighs, there he shall fall and none shall raise him, until all the evil is digested, for the Holy One, blessed be He, gives the wicked strength to endure their punishment, and for every single heating they collect from him anew. And the reason is as it is said (Genesis 39:10), "to lie beside her, to be with her" - and they said (Yoma 35b), "to lie beside her" in this world, "to be with her" in the World to Come, until he receives his punishment - as Rashbi, peace be upon him, said (Zohar, Parashat Pekudei, in the Chambers of Impurity, Chamber 2, page 263b), that there is his punishment, and we shall not copy its words - see there. And therefore his repentance is difficult, for he must do repentance for every single time he heated himself by emitting seed in vain.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:28: Further, my teacher, peace be upon him, wrote concerning "and Er, the firstborn of Judah, and Onan," of whom it is said, "and the LORD put them to death" - and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Tractate Kallah, chapter 3), from here that whoever emits seed in vain is liable for death by Heaven - and the reason is as explained above, that since that drop emitted in vain did not enter the female, the external force is immediately present there and takes that evil heat, and robs the soul that was fit to come through that drop - it follows that the external force holds all those souls fit to come through those drops. And when a person marries a woman and has not done the repentance proper, the external force presents there those pure, robbed souls held in her hand, and his children die while young, in the grip of their [demonic] mother, as explained in the Sabba (Parashat Mishpatim, page 96b). And in his grief over the death of his children, what he was liable for death by Heaven is atoned for him, since he too dies somewhat - provided he repents from then on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:29: And concerning this sin it is said (Jeremiah 2:34), "also on your skirts is found the blood of the souls of the innocent poor" - and so what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Niddah 13a), which we copied at the beginning of the chapter, "who slaughter the children" (Isaiah 57:5) - that this one actually slaughters his own children, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in Parashat Vayechi (page 219b), which we copied above. And therefore he does not see the face of the Shechinah, for the Shechinah is not revealed to him as she is revealed to other righteous ones, unless he does the proper repentance, as shall be explained - to this point is the summary of his intent.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:30: Further, concerning one who emits seed in vain, the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him (Zohar, Parashat Emor, page 90a) - these are its words: come and see, whoever emits seed in vain does not merit to see the face of the Shechinah and is called "evil," as it is said (Psalms 5:5), "for You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil shall not sojourn with You" - this refers to one who emits it by his hand or by other means; and if you say that this refers to emitting it into a wife who does not conceive - likewise it is so, no, but as we have said [it refers to deliberate waste] - and therefore a person should ask of the Holy One, blessed be He, to prepare for him a fit vessel, that he not blemish his seed - for whoever emits his seed into an unfit vessel blemishes his seed; woe to whoever blemishes his seed - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:31: And concerning the merit of one who is careful about emitting seed in vain, it is explained in Tanna DeVei Eliyahu, brought in the Yalkut, Parashat Mishpatim (siman 361, page 98, column 3), on the verse "and he sent the young men of the children of Israel, and they offered up burnt offerings" - these are its words: it is taught in the school of Eliyahu, this is what Scripture says (Deuteronomy 33:26), "there is none like the God of Yeshurun" - happy is a person who has words of Torah truly in him and from whom no seed has gone out in vain - and even if he is an ordinary Israelite, he is fit to offer up a burnt offering upon the altar like a High Priest, as it is said (Exodus 24:5), "and he sent the young men of the children of Israel." And whoever becomes lazy toward transgression and does not commit it is nourished by the radiance of the Shechinah, as it is said (Exodus 24:11), "and they beheld God, and ate and drank" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:32: And just as one must guard the covenant from emitting seed in vain, so one must guard it from a menstruant, a maidservant, a foreign woman, and a harlot - and this matter is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Beshalach, page 60b) - these are its words: Rabbi Yitzchak said, certainly whoever merits the Tzaddik merits Netzach and Hod, and these are the three by which Knesset Yisrael is blessed, and whoever merits them merits the Holy King, and enters into all four - and corresponding to these four, this holy sign is guarded from these four: the guarding of Knesset Yisrael is the guarding from a menstruant [niddah]; the guarding of Tzaddik is the guarding from a maidservant [shifchah]; the guarding of Netzach is the guarding from a foreign woman [nochriyah]; the guarding of Hod is the guarding from a harlot [zonah].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:33: And therefore, "to the voice of the LORD your God" - this is Knesset Yisrael, your God: through what do Israel merit to receive the face of the Shechinah? Through guarding from a menstruant - and therefore we have learned, it is written (Leviticus 18:19), "and you shall not approach a woman in the impurity of her menstruation to uncover her nakedness" - what is "to uncover her nakedness"? This is Knesset Yisrael, and through this other matters are held and bound, by which Knesset Yisrael is bound, and this has already been established.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:34: "And do what is right in His eyes" - this is Tzaddik, as it is written (Psalms 34:16), "the eyes of the LORD are toward the righteous" - to guard from a maidservant, and this matter has already been established, along the lines of (Proverbs 30:23), "and a maidservant when she inherits her mistress" - which causes the Tzaddik to cleave to the maidservant.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:35: "And you give ear to His commandments" - this is Netzach, to guard that he not deal falsely with it, that this sign not enter a foreign woman - "he shall not deal falsely with Netzach [eternity/victory]," as it is written (I Samuel 15:29), "and also the Netzach of Israel shall not lie" - and whoever guards this fulfills His commandments, as it is written (Exodus 34:14), "for you shall not bow to another god."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:36: "And keep all His statutes" - this is Hod, to guard from a harlot, and this follows as we have learned: Rabbi Yehudah said, what is the meaning of (Psalms 45:4), "gird your sword upon your thigh, mighty one, your glory [hodcha] and your splendor"? Rather, whoever girds himself and places the fear of a sharp, powerful sword against it, upon the thigh - what is "upon the thigh"? This is the holy sign, along the lines of (Genesis 24:2), "place, please, your hand under my thigh."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:37: Another explanation: "gird your sword" - meaning, be swift and strengthen yourself against your evil inclination, which is your sword, "upon the thigh" - upon that holy sign, to guard it; and if he guards it, he is then called "mighty," and the Holy One, blessed be He, clothes him in His own garments - and what are the garments of the Holy One, blessed be He? Hod and Netzach, as it is written (Psalms 104:1), "You are clothed in glory [hod] and splendor" - here too, "your glory [hodcha] and your splendor" - and then a person cleaves to the Holy King properly; from here onward, "all the illness that I placed upon Egypt I shall not place upon you, for I am the LORD your Healer" - to this point. Behold, from this teaching we learn the matter of guarding the covenant against these four mentioned.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:38: Now, included in the guarding from a menstruant, one must be careful not to touch her, as the decisors have elaborated at length on this - and therefore one must instruct the woman in the laws of menstrual impurity, the wearing of a white garment and its changing, and the laws of interposition [chatzitzah] and immersion, since there are several matters the woman may not know, and thus find herself having relations while a menstruant [unknowingly]. And it is possible that Rashbi, peace be upon him, intended this in the teaching concerning the matter of the menstruant, saying, "and through this other matters are held and bound, by which Knesset Yisrael is bound."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:39: Also, the teaching explains the merit of one who guards the covenant, who is called "mighty," and his merit in the World to Come, that the Holy One, blessed be He, clothes him in His own garments, which are Netzach and Hod. And likewise his merit, as it says at the end of the teaching, "and then a person cleaves to the Holy King" - this is Tiferet - and there is fulfilled in him the end of the verse, "all the illness that I placed upon Egypt," and so on, "for I am the LORD your Healer" - for since he cleaves to the Holy King, he draws healing from Arich Anpin, and from the affirmative you infer the negative, God forbid [i.e., the converse also holds for one who does not guard the covenant].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:40: And so in the Midrash Yalkut they expounded the verse (Song of Songs 3:8), "each man with his sword upon his thigh," concerning the warning of the covenant - these are its words: another explanation, "each man with his sword upon his thigh" - this is circumcision; "because of dread in the nights" - that they are careful of sin, which is compared to the night - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:41: And concerning the blemish of the covenant with a married woman, or one who comes upon a menstruant, maidservant, foreign woman, or harlot, it is explained in the Zohar and in the Midrashim of our Rabbis, concerning the blemish of the covenant with a married woman, or one who comes upon a menstruant, maidservant, foreign woman, or harlot - we have seen fit to copy some of their words, so that the sinner shall fear upon hearing the punishment.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:42: They said in Midrash Rabbah, Parashat Ki Tisa (Bamidbar Rabbah 9:7), on the verse (Micah 2:10), "arise and go, for this is not the resting place; because of impurity, it shall destroy, and with a severe destruction" - the Holy One, blessed be He, said to them, for other transgressions I would be patient with you, but since you have spread out in adultery, arise and go. What is "and a severe destruction" [chevel namratz]? I said (Deuteronomy 32:9), "for the LORD's portion is His people, Jacob is the cord [chevel] of His inheritance" - I took Jacob, and he was My portion, since his seed resembled a cord that is chained one to another, for they were all genealogically linked, children of their [proper] fathers, and no other seed interrupted between them, since they all guarded themselves from adultery and there was no illegitimacy there - how so? It is written (I Chronicles 5:30), "Elazar begot Pinchas, and Pinchas begot Avishua," and so on for all of them, and the chain came in this way - but you entered upon your fellow's wife and defiled the inheritance: how shall he count "so-and-so, my son," when he is not his son, being a mamzer - you severed the cord [chevel] - hence "and a severe destruction" [chevel namratz]. What is NAMRATZ? An acrostic: adulterer [No'ef], bastard [Mamzer], wicked [Rasha], oppressor [Tzorer]. From here you learn, concerning the Ten Tribes, that their sentence was sealed only for the sin of adultery.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:43: And from where do we know concerning the tribe of Judah and Benjamin that their sentence was sealed only for adultery? For so Jeremiah cried out before God: in the days of Manasseh the sons were the sons of their [proper] fathers, now they are children of lewdness - this is what is written (Jeremiah 4:22), "for My people are foolish," and so on; what is written at the end of the passage? (ibid. 5:8), "they were like well-fed horses roaming free, each neighing after his neighbor's wife" - although they transgressed all the commandments and denied the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is written (ibid. 5:12), "they have denied the LORD" - He is patient; but for adultery their sentence was sealed against them, for it is written after it (ibid. 5:9), "shall I not punish these things, says the LORD?" The Holy One, blessed be He, said, for everything else I suppress [My anger], but for lewdness I am angered - behold, I hand them over to kingdoms, this is what is written (ibid. 5:10), "go up upon her vine-rows and destroy" - to this point. Further, later in the same passage (Bamidbar Rabbah 9:12): they transgress the Ten Commandments - and so it is said (Ecclesiastes 7:26), "and I find more bitter than death the woman" - woe to the transgression through which the Ten Commandments are transgressed - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:44: And in Bereishit Rabbah (chapter 26:5) - these are its words: Rabbi Simlai said, wherever you find licentiousness, indiscriminate slaughter [andralamusia] comes to the world and kills both evil and good. Rabbi Azariah and Rabbi Yehudah bar Rabbi Simon in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said, for everything the Holy One, blessed be He, is patient, except for licentiousness, as it is said (Genesis 6:2), "and the sons of God saw," and so on; what is written after it? (ibid. 6:7), "and the LORD said, I will blot out man." Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said in the name of Rabbi Pedaya, all that night Lot was seeking mercy for the people of Sodom and they were accepting it from him; once they said to him (Genesis 19:5), "bring them out to us, that we may know them" - for relations - they said to him (ibid. 19:12), "who else do you have here? Son-in-law..." - to teach a defense; from then on you have no one to teach a defense for them - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:45: And in Bava Metzia (58b) we say, three go down to Gehinnom and do not come up, and these are they: one who gives his fellow a bad name, one who shames his fellow publicly, and one who comes upon a married woman - to this point.
